name: Soreng
tagline: A farming district town with a sunrise hill above the bazaar
meta_description: Soreng, headquarters of Sikkim's sixth district: Chuli Dara sunrise, Ramidham, Sribadam monasteries, orange orchards, how to get there and honest costs.
summary: Soreng is the headquarters of Soreng district, a hill bazaar at about 1,300 m roughly 28 km above Jorethang and 100 km from Siliguri. It is a working town, not a resort: come for the Chuli Dara sunrise walk, Ramidham's hilltop view, the Sribadam monasteries, orange and cardamom farms and cheap, practical rooms.
intro: Soreng town spreads up a steep slope in the south-west of Sikkim, about 28 km and a little over an hour above Jorethang. Until December 2021 it was a subdivision of West Sikkim; it is now the headquarters of Soreng district, the state's sixth, with the district offices, a hospital, banks, schools and the shared-jeep stand all within a short walk of the bazaar. The district administration gives the town's altitude as about 4,314 ft, roughly 1,300 m, though upper wards climb well above that.

Most travellers pass through Soreng on the way to Rinchenpong, Kaluk or Okhrey, and that is a fair way to use it. But a night here repays an early riser. The district site lists Chuli Dara, a hilltop about 45 minutes on foot above town, for sunrise, and on clear mornings you look across Sikkim and south to the Darjeeling hills. Ramidham, a Hindu hilltop shrine about 13–14 km away, has a wide Kangchenjunga view, and the Sribadam monasteries are a short drive north.

Soreng is farming country. Wikipedia and the district site both note oranges, ginger, large cardamom, vegetables and flowers as the main crops, and from November to January the orange trees around the houses turn the slopes orange and green. The town itself is plain and busy in the mornings. Expect simple hotels and homestays, momo and thali eateries and few other visitors, at prices well below Pelling.

story.title: How a West Sikkim subdivision became a district
story.text: For most of its modern history Soreng was a subdivision of the West district, run from Gyalshing. On 13 December 2021 the state government notified two new districts, Soreng and Pakyong, under notification number 26/L&PAD/2021, and the West district was split into Gyalshing and Soreng. Soreng town became the headquarters. The district administration describes the new district as lying in the south-west corner of the state, sharing a border with West Bengal to the south and an international border with Nepal to the west, with the Akar bridge at Jorethang as its entry point from Namchi district. It has two subdivisions, Soreng and Mangalbarey, and six blocks: Baiguney, Kaluk, Daramdin, Mangalbarey, Chumbong and Soreng. For travellers the change is mostly one of names on signboards, but it brought new offices, a district hospital and more attention to places like Barsey, Rinchenpong and Tharpu that used to sit at the far end of West Sikkim's tourist map.
story.source: Soreng district administration, soreng.nic.in (About District; Subdivision and Blocks; A Brief Resume of District); Wikipedia: Soreng district

little_known.fact: The district site lists Chuli Dara, a hilltop about 45 minutes' walk above Soreng town, as a sunrise point from which you can see much of Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills to the south.
At Jor Pokhari in Phuncheybong, between Soreng and Sribadam, people say there were once two lakes, male and female, and that the male lake moved to Khecheopalri. A temple was built there in 1999.
little_known.source: soreng.nic.in (Jor Pokhari Mandir); as told locally

little_known.fact: Payul Dechen Gaweling Monastery near Sribadam is young by Sikkim standards: the district site says it was founded in 2006 by Payul Lathul Rinpoche and follows the Nyingma school.

highlights.title: Chuli Dara at sunrise
highlights.text: A hilltop viewpoint about 45 minutes on foot above Soreng town, listed by the district administration for sunrise. On clear mornings from October to April you see across western and southern Sikkim and to the Darjeeling hills. Start in the dark with a torch and a warm layer, and ask the way in town.

highlights.title: Ramidham hilltop shrine
highlights.text: A Hindu religious site above Bara Samdong, about 13–14 km from Soreng and 2.5 km uphill from the Kaluk–Soreng road. The district site describes a Kangchenjunga view, a sacred pond called Sakundhara and a Saptami Puja held twice a year. Go early for the mountains.

highlights.title: Sribadam monasteries
highlights.text: North of town on the road to Kaluk, Sribadam has Phuntsok Choeling, a Kagyu monastery the district counts among its oldest, and Payul Dechen Gaweling, a large Nyingma monastery founded in 2006 where monks pray at about 6 am and 4 pm. Dress modestly and ask before photographing.

highlights.title: Jor Pokhari
highlights.text: A small natural pond and temple at Phuncheybong between Soreng and Sribadam. As told locally and on the district site, a male lake once lay beside the surviving female lake before moving to Khecheopalri. The temple dates from 1999. A quiet half-hour stop on the Sribadam drive.

highlights.title: Bazaar mornings and orange season
highlights.text: Soreng bazaar is busiest from about 6 to 10 am, when jeeps load for Jorethang and Siliguri and farmers bring vegetables, ginger and, from November to January, oranges. It is a good place to eat a cheap breakfast, buy fruit and see the district at work.

highlights.title: A practical overnight
highlights.text: Soreng has what Rinchenpong and Okhrey lack: ATMs, pharmacies, a district hospital and frequent shared jeeps. That makes it a sensible halfway night between the Rinchenpong ridge and the Barsey side, or a base for Tharpu, Daramdin and Mangardzong in the lower valleys.

how_to_reach.text: Shared jeeps run from Jorethang to Soreng through the day, about 1–1.5 hours for roughly ₹80–150 a seat. From Siliguri, a few jeeps run direct to Soreng in the morning, about 4 hours, otherwise change at Jorethang. The stand in Soreng bazaar also has jeeps for Daramdin, Sombaria, Kaluk and Rinchenpong.

Soreng is about 28 km from Jorethang via the Akar bridge and Nayabazar, 18 km from Rinchenpong and about 30 km from Okhrey via Sombaria. From Gangtok allow 4.5–5 hours for about 115 km via Melli and Jorethang. A small car from Gangtok costs about ₹5,000–6,000 one way.

The district gives NJP as about 115 km and Bagdogra about 125–130 km from Soreng, 4–5 hours by car via Sevoke, Melli and Jorethang, about ₹4,500–6,000 for a small car. NH10 along the Teesta closes after monsoon slides; drivers then go via Kalimpong or Darjeeling. Check current status before you travel.

where_to_stay: Soreng has a handful of plain town hotels and family homestays rather than resorts. The Orchid Hotel at Pragati Chowk is one of the hotels the district administration lists, at about ₹1,500–3,000 a room. The district site also lists Hotel Ghakhil and homestays such as Senin and Mustang for the Chuli Dara side; confirm they are operating when you book. For views and quiet, most travellers sleep 18 km away in Rinchenpong or Kaluk, or 30 km away in Okhrey, and see Soreng on the way.
tips: Use Soreng's ATMs before heading to Rinchenpong, Okhrey or Hilley, where machines are rare or absent.
For Chuli Dara, leave town about an hour before sunrise with a torch and ask a local for the path the evening before.
Shared jeeps to Jorethang and Siliguri leave mostly in the early morning; after midday they thin out.
Buy oranges in the bazaar from November to January, when Soreng's orchards are at their best.
Treat Soreng as a one-night stop or a lunch break, and spend more nights on the Rinchenpong ridge or in Okhrey.

experiences.title: Sunrise hike to Chuli Dara above Soreng
experiences.summary: Walk about 45 minutes uphill from Soreng town in the dark to Chuli Dara, a hilltop the district lists for sunrise, and watch first light reach the Kangchenjunga range and the hills of Sikkim and Darjeeling. Free, quiet and best from October to April.
body: Chuli Dara is a hilltop above Soreng town that the district administration lists as a sunrise and hiking point. The walk up takes about 45 minutes from town on village paths and steps, steep in places. Leave about an hour before sunrise, which is around 6:15–6:30 am in December and January and about 5:00 am in May, so that you reach the top as the sky lightens. A torch, a warm jacket and shoes with grip are all you need.

From the top, on a clear morning, the view runs north to the snow peaks and south across the Rangeet valley to the Darjeeling hills, with the farms and villages of Soreng district laid out below. October to December gives the clearest air; February to April is often hazier, with rhododendron and magnolia flowering on the higher slopes. From June to September cloud usually hides everything, so do not plan the walk around monsoon views.

There are no facilities at Chuli Dara, so carry water and a snack, and bring your rubbish back down. Ask your hotel or homestay the evening before which path to take, since several lanes leave the bazaar. If you prefer company, a local guide costs about ₹500–800 for the morning. Back in town, the breakfast places near the jeep stand open early.

faqs.q: How long is the walk to Chuli Dara from Soreng?
faqs.a: About 45 minutes uphill from Soreng town, according to the district administration, and a little less coming down. The path uses village lanes and steps and is steep in places. Allow about 2.5 hours for the round trip with time at the top, and start in the dark if you want the sunrise.

faqs.q: Can you see Kangchenjunga from Chuli Dara?
faqs.a: On clear mornings, yes, mostly from October to April. The district site highlights the wide view over Sikkim and towards Darjeeling. Cloud often builds by 8–9 am, so the first hour after sunrise is the best time. From June to September the mountains are usually hidden.

faqs.q: Is the Chuli Dara hike safe in the dark?
faqs.a: It is a village path, not a wild trail, but it is steep and uneven. Carry a good torch, wear shoes with grip and confirm the route with your hotel the evening before. If you are unsure, go with a local guide for about ₹500–800, or start at first light instead.

experiences.title: Ramidham hilltop shrine and Kangchenjunga view
experiences.summary: Drive about 13–14 km from Soreng and walk 2.5 km uphill to Ramidham, a Hindu hilltop site above Bara Samdong with a sacred pond, a twice-yearly Saptami Puja and, on clear mornings, a wide view of Kangchenjunga.
body: Ramidham sits on a hilltop above Bara Samdong, about 13–14 km from Soreng. The district administration describes it as a religious site where the name means holy and blissful, reached by a 2.5 km uphill walk from the Kaluk–Soreng road at Samdong. The walk climbs through rhododendron, chestnut and magnolia, and takes 45 minutes to an hour at a steady pace. There are several temples and small shrines at the top.

The district site mentions a sacred pond called Sakundhara, which, according to local belief, a sadhu created when there was no water on the hill. It also notes a Saptami Puja held twice a year, when people gather to pray for world peace, and government work on the site, including a statue the district describes as of the first Limboo teacher and a traditional house. Treat the shrines as places of worship: remove shoes where asked and keep voices low.

Come for the morning view too. From the top, the Kangchenjunga range spreads across the north on clear days from October to April, and much of western Sikkim lies below. A small car from Soreng for the half day costs about ₹1,500–2,000; it can also be done from Kaluk. Carry water, as there are few shops at the top, and check the Saptami Puja dates locally if you want to see it.

faqs.q: How do I reach Ramidham from Soreng?
faqs.a: Drive about 13–14 km along the Kaluk–Soreng road to Samdong, then walk about 2.5 km uphill to the top, as the district administration describes it. A small car from Soreng for the half day costs about ₹1,500–2,000. The walk takes 45 minutes to an hour for most people.

faqs.q: When is the Saptami Puja at Ramidham?
faqs.a: The district site says it is held twice a year, but dates follow the Hindu calendar and are set locally. Ask in Soreng or Kaluk, or ask us, a few weeks before your trip. On puja days expect crowds from nearby villages and more vehicles on the access road.

faqs.q: Is Ramidham suitable for older travellers?
faqs.a: The 2.5 km climb is steady rather than difficult, so most fit seniors manage it slowly with rests. There are no ponies or vehicles beyond the road. If walking uphill is a problem, enjoy the views from the road at Samdong and the Kaluk ridge instead.

experiences.title: Sribadam monasteries and Jor Pokhari half-day
experiences.cost: Small car ≈ ₹1,500–2,500 for the half day
experiences.summary: A half-day drive north of Soreng to the Jor Pokhari pond and temple at Phuncheybong, the old Kagyu monastery of Phuntsok Choeling and the large Nyingma monastery of Payul Dechen Gaweling, founded in 2006. Time it for morning prayers.
body: Start at Jor Pokhari in Phuncheybong, between Soreng and Sribadam. The district administration describes it as a site of natural and spiritual importance, with naturally formed ponds and a cave, and a temple built in 1999. The story told here, which the district site repeats, is that there were once two lakes, male and female, and that the male lake moved to Khecheopalri, the sacred lake near Pelling, leaving only the female lake. We tell it as local belief.

In Sribadam, Phuntsok Choeling is a Kagyu monastery that the district site names among the oldest in Soreng district. Close by, Payul Dechen Gaweling is a newer and much larger Nyingma monastery, founded in 2006 by Payul Lathul Rinpoche according to the district, with daily prayers at about 6 am and 4 pm. The district notes the Losoong festival and a December cham dance here; dates follow the Tibetan calendar, so check current status before you travel.

A small car from Soreng for four hours costs about ₹1,500–2,500, and the route can continue to Kaluk and Rinchenpong if you are moving on. Walk clockwise around shrines, remove shoes before entering, and ask before photographing monks or images. Parts of Payul Dechen Gaweling have been under renovation, so some halls may be closed.

faqs.q: How far is Sribadam from Soreng?
faqs.a: Sribadam lies north of Soreng on the road towards Kaluk and Rinchenpong, roughly 30–40 minutes by car with stops. Jor Pokhari at Phuncheybong is on the way. If you are travelling between Soreng and Rinchenpong anyway, the monasteries make an easy break in the journey.

faqs.q: Can visitors attend prayers at Payul Dechen Gaweling Monastery?
faqs.a: Visitors can usually watch quietly from the back. The district site says monks pray daily from about 6 am and 4 pm. Sit where you are shown, switch phones to silent, do not use flash and leave a small offering if you wish. Ask before taking any photographs.

faqs.q: What is the story of Jor Pokhari?
faqs.a: Jor means pair in Nepali. As told locally and recorded on the Soreng district site, there were once two lakes here, male and female, and the male lake moved to Khecheopalri, leaving the female lake behind. A temple was built at the site in 1999, and people from nearby villages come to pray.

experiences.title: Soreng bazaar morning in orange season
experiences.summary: Spend an early morning in Soreng bazaar as the jeeps load and farmers bring in vegetables, ginger and cardamom. From November to January buy Sikkim mandarins straight from growers, then eat a cheap breakfast of momos, sel roti or puri-sabzi.
body: Soreng is a farming district, and its bazaar shows it best in the first hours of the day. From about 6 am jeeps line up for Jorethang and Siliguri, and growers arrive with sacks of vegetables, ginger, beans and seasonal fruit. Wikipedia and the district site both name oranges, ginger, large cardamom, vegetables and flowers as Soreng's main crops, and the district notes that farming here is organic, as it is across Sikkim.

From November to January the Sikkim mandarin is in season. The district economy page calls it the most important commercial fruit of the state, a loose-skinned orange similar to the Darjeeling mandarin. You will see it in baskets at the bazaar and on trees around houses all the way down the road. Prices vary with the harvest; expect roughly ₹10–20 a fruit in a good year, more early in the season.

For breakfast, the small eateries near the jeep stand serve momos, chowmein, puri with potato curry and, at some places, sel roti, the ring-shaped rice bread, with tea for about ₹100–200. This is not a guided tour: wander, buy what looks good, and ask before photographing people or their stalls. Carry small notes, as UPI depends on the mobile signal.

faqs.q: When are oranges in season in Soreng?
faqs.a: Roughly November to January, with the best fruit in December. The Soreng district site lists the Sikkim mandarin among the district's key organic cash crops. Outside that window you will still find ginger, vegetables and other seasonal produce in the bazaar, but not the orange-heavy stalls of winter.

faqs.q: Is there a weekly market day in Soreng?
faqs.a: Soreng bazaar trades every day, and mornings are always busiest. Some villages in the district hold weekly haats on fixed days, and market days can change, so ask your hotel or driver which days are busiest during your stay. Early morning is the best time whatever the day.

faqs.q: What should I eat for breakfast in Soreng?
faqs.a: Momos, puri with potato curry, chowmein and tea are easy to find near the jeep stand for about ₹100–200. Some places make sel roti, a ring-shaped fried rice bread popular in Nepali households. Eat early, before the jeeps leave and the busiest stalls run out.

faqs.q: Is Soreng worth visiting?
faqs.a: As a base or a one-night stop, yes. Soreng is the district headquarters, with ATMs, a hospital and shared jeeps, plus the Chuli Dara sunrise walk, Ramidham and the Sribadam monasteries nearby. For views and quiet, though, most travellers prefer to sleep in Rinchenpong, Kaluk or Okhrey and pass through Soreng.

faqs.q: How far is Soreng from Siliguri and NJP?
faqs.a: The district administration gives about 100 km from Siliguri and 115 km from NJP, roughly 4–5 hours by car via Sevoke, Melli and Jorethang. NH10 along the Teesta closes after monsoon slides, when drivers go via Kalimpong or Darjeeling instead. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Soreng from Gangtok?
faqs.a: About 115 km by road via Singtam, Melli and Jorethang, or via Namchi, usually 4.5–5 hours. A small car costs about ₹5,000–6,000 one way. There is no direct shared jeep we would rely on; most people change at Jorethang.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to visit Soreng?
faqs.a: Indian nationals do not need a special permit for Soreng. Foreign nationals need Sikkim's Restricted Area Permit, which since January 2026 is applied for online on the e-FRRO portal after arriving in India. Sikkim also charges a ₹50 tourist fee, collected by hotels. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Soreng?
faqs.a: October to December for clear Kangchenjunga views and dry, mild days of about 15–22 °C, and February to April for flowering trees and the Barsey rhododendrons nearby. January is cold but often clear. June to September brings heavy rain and landslides, so we avoid it for sightseeing.

faqs.q: What is the altitude of Soreng?
faqs.a: The district administration gives about 4,314 ft, roughly 1,300 m, for the town, though it spreads up a steep slope and upper wards are higher. That is low enough that altitude sickness is not a concern. Nights fall to about 3–6 °C in winter, so pack warm layers.

faqs.q: Are there ATMs in Soreng?
faqs.a: Yes, Soreng bazaar has bank ATMs, and it is the best place to draw cash before going on to Rinchenpong, Kaluk, Okhrey or Hilley, where machines are rare. ATMs can run dry over long weekends and holidays, so carry a reserve of cash from Siliguri or Jorethang too.

faqs.q: Can I do Soreng as a day trip from Pelling?
faqs.a: You can drive through, but it is a long day. Pelling to Soreng is roughly 2–2.5 hours each way via Legship and Kaluk. It makes more sense to move on from Pelling to Rinchenpong or Kaluk and see Soreng, Sribadam and Ramidham from there.

faqs.q: What is Soreng known for?
faqs.a: Soreng is known as the headquarters of Sikkim's newest district, created in December 2021, and for farming: oranges, ginger, large cardamom, vegetables and flowers. For visitors it is the gateway to Rinchenpong, Kaluk, Okhrey and the Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary, and has its own sunrise walk at Chuli Dara.
